title: Andes: Defining and Enhancing Quality-of-Experience in LLM-Based Text Streaming Services
technique: QoE-aware token-level preemptive scheduler (knapsack formulation, priority by QoE gain per resource) + client-side token pacer

optimized_metrics.evidence: Its objective is to maximize the average QoE across all requests.
total weight (context length) does not exceed the knapsack's capacity (GPU memory)

headline_claim.text: compared to state-of-the-art LLM serving systems, Andes improves the average QoE by up to 4.7x given the same GPU resource, or saves up to 61% GPU resources while maintaining the same high QoE

reported_metrics.where: resource savings % GPUs for avg QoE 0.95
headline only (re-pass); resource saving is a result of the QoE objective, no design statement

metric_definitions.definition_quote: QoE = 1 - S_delay / S_whole  (Eq. 3), with S_delay = sum_{i=1..n} (T_i^Actual - T_i^Ideal) (Eq. 1) and S_whole = sum_{i=1..n} (T_n^Actual - T_i^Ideal) (Eq. 2)
metric_definitions.notes: in [0,1]; 1 = every token delivered no later than the ideal consumption timeline (TTFT target + constant reading-speed TDS); 0 = no tokens arrive. Computed per request over the whole timeline; reported as average (and CDF).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: During the former phase, time-to-first-token (TTFT) matters; the first token should be delivered to users before they lose patience. The target TTFT should depend on the service, be it constant or proportional to the prompt length.
metric_definitions.notes: not formally defined as arrival-to-first-token, but includes queueing in practice (HOL blocking inflates TTFT)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: users expect the server's token delivery speed (TDS) to match their consumption speed
metric_definitions.notes: tokens/s delivered; equals 1/TPOT-like quantity per request; faster than reading speed gives no benefit

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Average QoE: The QoE value of requests when they finish, averaged across all requests.
Resource savings (%): How much fewer GPUs Andes needs to maintain an average QoE of 0.95.
metric_definitions.notes: target avg QoE 0.95 is the quality bar

slo_spec: No SLO per se; QoE parameters per request (TTFT target and expected token delivery speed, e.g. reading speed; tiers of speeds). Quality bar avg QoE >= 0.95 for resource-saving claim.
load_regime: trace replay (one-hour slice of BurstGPT with multi-round ShareGPT lengths) plus synthetic bursty arrivals (burst intensity/duration swept)
tradeoff_acknowledged: favours QoE over raw throughput ('Throughput is not all you need'); preemption overhead (swap/recompute) handled via refiner; paper argues TTFT/TPOT/P99 statistics miss user experience
hardware: AWS p4d.24xlarge, A100 x4 or x8
models: Phi-3-mini 3.8B, Command R 32B, Phi-3.5-MoE 16x3.8B (and others in Table 1)
workloads: BurstGPT-timed arrivals, Multi-Round ShareGPT lengths, synthetic bursts
extractor_notes: Critiques standard metrics: server-centric throughput, TTFT, and avg/P90/P99 TPOT 'fail to fully capture user experience'. Optimizes the MEAN of per-request QoE, not tail or percentile. Appendix A mentions alternative objectives (e.g. minimum QoE) not read in detail. Baselines vLLM v0.6.1 and Sarathi-Serve.
load_class_quote: We leverage both real-world request traces from BurstGPT [34] and synthetic bursty traces (§6.1)
repass_log: COST: moved to reported (headline-only; QoE remains the objective)
